headline: Computational tools extract single-cell and spatial features from imaging and omics data
label: Single Cell Imaging Analysis Tools
summary: Recent preprints and publications report interpretable, scalable tools for quantifying single-cell morphology, dynamics, and spatial heterogeneity.
synthesis: The items share computational extraction of quantitative information from single-cell and spatial measurements, though modalities differ. MORPHIS derives compact, interpretable morphological signatures from microscopy images to quantify single-cell treatment and aging responses. NetTracer3D provides an open tool for 3D tissue maps, with connectivity, branch adjacency, and proximity network analyses. SMART and 3d-OT address spatial multi-omics integration via graph neural networks with metric learning and geometry-aware optimal transport, respectively. A lipid-dynamics study infers longitudinal single-cell behavior from one destructive measurement, and a review catalogs image-based profiling stages. What is new is interpretable morphological signatures and geometry-aware alignment applied to spatially resolved single-cell data.
